newsitem.title: UK: Labour will try to force early UK election.
newsitem.headline: Labour will try to force early UK election.

text.p: The main British opposition Labour party said on Monday that it would do all it could to force an early general election.
Labour leader Tony Blair told a news conference: "It is time to leave the tired, decaying Tories behind. That is why we will do all we can to force an early election."
Blair was announcing the results of a ballot in which 61 percent of the party (380,688 members) voted by a margin of 19 to 1 to approve its pre-election blueprint "New Labour, New Life for Britain".

Blair said the turnout for the ballot was higher than in last year's vote on new wording for the party's constitution. "This is an important day for the Labour party and an important day for Britain," Blair said.
"This is the party's covenant with the people. It is our mandate to stand as new Labour and to govern as new Labour. What the people see is what the people will get."

Blair was speaking a day after Prime Minister John Major's majority in 651-seat House of Commons (lower house) fell to one following the death of Conservative member of parliament Barry Porter. Major must hold an election by May 22, 1997.

Blair said the huge endorsement of his programme gave Labour the best possible platform in the run-up to the election. "Today I am saying to every member of the party: "It is time to raise our game once more. It is time to build on our success and step up a gear'."
